question: Which Linux companion app implementation path should OpenClaw sponsor for this umbrella issue now that Windows Hub is shipped?
rationale: Current main has no Linux companion app, while multiple open implementation tracks differ in language, dependency stack, packaging model, and security boundary; automation cannot safely choose that product and ownership direction.

options.title: Sponsor one native Linux track
options.body: Choose one Linux app architecture, assign reviewers for security/packaging/API boundaries, and use the selected PR as the canonical implementation path.

options.title: Split Linux parity into narrow issues
options.body: Keep this umbrella open but move tray, setup, chat, node capabilities, packaging, and notifications into separately reviewable Linux follow-ups before accepting a large app PR.

options.title: Defer Linux companion work
options.body: Leave Linux on the supported Gateway/CLI path for now and close or pause broad Linux app PRs until security and setup priorities have capacity.

recommendation.title: Sponsor one native Linux track
recommendation.body: Choose one Linux app architecture, assign reviewers for security/packaging/API boundaries, and use the selected PR as the canonical implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete opened the umbrella issue, gave the strongest product-direction comments in the discussion, and appears in recent platform documentation history.
